articles.title: Louisiana girl, 8, dies after contracting suspected brain-eating amoeba linked to lake swim
articles.summary: Lillian Smart's family says the 8-year-old's brain injuries were too severe to survive after contracting Naegleria fowleri while swimming in a lake.
articles.body: Lillian Smart, an 8-year-old girl who health officials believe contracted a brain-eating amoeba while swimming in a northern Louisiana lake, died Saturday at a Ruston hospital from an infection linked to the pathogen. Lillian died one day after celebrating her eighth birthday. "The injuries to her brain were too severe for her little body to recover from," the Smart family said in a statement posted Sunday morning on Facebook. "Everyone did everything they could to keep her here. We are heartbroken and honestly do not know what to do next. How do we put one foot in front of the other without our girl?" The Louisiana Department of Health announced Wednesday that a state resident had been hospitalized after becoming infected with Naegleria fowleri, a microscopic amoeba that can cause a rare and often deadly brain infection. MICHIGAN REPORTS 2 DEATHS IN RARE PARASITE OUTBREAK THAT HAS SICKENED MORE THAN 11,000 State health officials have not publicly identified Lillian as the patient referenced in the announcement. Her family, however, said on social media that she had been admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit at a Ruston hospital and identified Naegleria fowleri as the cause of her illness. The health department said the infection in the case it announced was most likely acquired while the patient was swimming in Lake Claiborne shortly before becoming ill. A representative for the Louisiana Department of Health did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Louisiana Department of Health records identify three previous deaths associated with Naegleria fowleri in the state since 2011. BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE Two happened in 2011. A 20-year-old man in St. Bernard Parish died after using tap water to rinse his sinuses, while a 51-year-old woman in DeSoto Parish died after using tap water for a similar purpose. In 2013, a 4-year-old boy contracted the amoeba while visiting a home in St. Bernard Parish, where he had played on a slip-and-slide. State officials later reported that CDC testing detected Naegleria fowleri in the parish water system. Naegleria fowleri causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, or PAM, an extremely rare brain infection that can develop when contaminated water enters the nose and the amoeba travels to the brain. People cannot become infected by swallowing contaminated water. The amoeba is not found in saltwater or properly chlorinated swimming pools. DEADLY BACTERIA FOUND IN WATERS NEAR LUXURY VACATION DESTINATION AHEAD OF SUMMER Symptoms typically begin with headache, fever, nausea and vomiting before progressing to a stiff neck, seizures and coma. Symptoms generally appear about five days after infection, and the disease can lead to death within about one to two weeks. About 97% of people who develop PAM die from the infection, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The CDC reported two PAM cases nationwide last year. Of the 173 infections documented over roughly the past 90 years, nearly 91% occurred in July and August.

articles.title: Four ways to make sure your will protects your family and avoids added grief
articles.summary: An estate planning attorney can ensure your will meets state-specific requirements, but making it findable is just as critical for your loved ones.
articles.body: There is no worse feeling in life than when a loved one passes away. And when that individual has not communicated his or her wishes or shared key information, that can add an additional burden of time, money and stress to loved ones’ grief. As August is National Make a Will Month, here are four suggestions to help you make sure you have your will made and updated in a manner that will help your loved ones sort through your estate and continue your legacy in the best manner possible. Make your will today! CEO’S FIRE DEATH SPARKS MYSTERY, WILL FIGHT OVER TECH TITAN'S FORTUNE When it comes to estate planning, having a will is important. Having one that is done properly is more important. There are online services that can help you, but I recommend meeting with a local estate planning attorney. Not only will a professional make sure that your wishes are accounted for properly, but they will understand state-specific requirements and regulations. Moreover, many estate planning attorneys can help with more than just the legal aspects of estate planning; they can also help or find you someone to help with tax planning and any related entities, such as trusts, to make sure your assets are passed down in the most tax-efficient manner. Explore making gifts and other plans now RICKY GERVAIS JOKES UK INHERITANCE TAX MAY FINALLY PUSH HIM TO MARRY LONGTIME PARTNER AFTER 40 YEARS As you meet with an estate planning professional or your accountant, you can explore making gifts to loved ones today. This may bring you more satisfaction, so that you can see your loved ones benefit from what you plan to leave them instead of waiting until you are gone. In 2026, you can gift $19,000 individually ($38,000 for married couples) per person, tax free for the year. Again, consult a professional for assistance to make sure you are crossing all your "t’s" and dotting your "is" regarding any gifting. Also, if you have family members who can handle the discussion, dividing up possessions, whether passed now or later, as a family can help minimize fighting among family members down the road. Moreover, many in the younger generations aren’t interested in the same physical mementos as those who are older. If you have a china set or a collection of statues that hasn’t been used in years, and nobody in the family wants them, you can explore making plans for disposal now – whether that means selling or donating the items. This can generate extra cash, tax deductions or even find a home with someone who you know will enjoy them. As a bonus, it will create less "cleanup" down the road for loved ones. Make your will findable MAN ACCUSED OF STEALING MORE THAN $735K AS POWER OF ATTORNEY TO PURCHASE PROPERTY, ONLYFANS AND LIFE COACHING One of the biggest issues I have seen with those who have wills is that their loved ones can’t find it (or don’t know which is the most recent copy). Preparing your wishes and information but not making them accessible to your loved ones defeats the purpose. Put your will, along with other key information (like a listing of your financial accounts and advisors or a key to your safe deposit box) and any personal wishes in a legacy and wishes planning kit. You can use one like the kit I created after my father’s passing, Future File, or you can make your own if you prefer. As you meet with an estate planning professional or your accountant, you can explore making gifts to loved ones today. This may bring you more satisfaction, so that you can see your loved ones benefit from what you plan to leave them instead of waiting until you are gone. Whichever route you go, make sure your family members either have access to your kit and its contents now or know how to access it and can do so in case of an emergency or if you pass. Review your will regularly OLIVER TREE MADE EERIE COMMENTS ABOUT HIS WILL WEEKS BEFORE FATAL HELICOPTER CRASH IN RIO DE JANEIRO A friend of mine’s mother was gravely ill and told my friend about her will. When my friend had an estate planning attorney review it, it turned out that it did not reflect what her mother’s current wishes were; rather, it contained some changes other family members had suggested many years ago that her mother had forgotten about. If this hadn’t been reviewed, her mother would not have left her assets to her grandchildren, but rather to distant cousins. That underscores why it is important to review your will regularly and make any updates if circumstances change over the years. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Additionally, if you have financial accounts, retirement plans or policies, such as insurance policies, that have beneficiaries, make sure that those are up to date, accurate and match your wishes. Beneficiary designations supersede wills, and so beneficiaries will receive the payments, even if they differ from your will. Check this on a regular basis as you review and update your will. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Saving your loved ones dozens of hours of time, giving them peace of mind and reducing uncertainty and even infighting during a very difficult time are the best things that you can leave behind as part of your legacy. That only happens with the proper planning today. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM CAROL ROTH

articles.title: 'Perfect' workout formula can take just 10 minutes a day, Hilaria Baldwin says
articles.summary: Hilaria Baldwin shares her "perfect" workout trifecta of cardio, strength training and stretching, plus tips for building exercise consistency.
articles.body: Being motivated to work out is one thing, but staying committed to a routine is what yields results, experts say. In an interview with Fox News Digital, certified yoga and fitness instructor Hilaria Baldwin shared her tips for building an effective exercise routine – and sticking to it. "One of the most important things about exercise is consistency," said the mother of seven. "For many of us, life gets in the way – we are parents and we work and all the chaos comes in, so bite-sized movements are really important." CHIEFS HEIRESS GRACIE HUNT REVEALS WHY SHE LIFTS HEAVY WEIGHTS — AND DOESN’T COUNT CALORIES Baldwin revealed that her "perfect" workout routine trifecta always includes cardio, strength training and stretching, even if it’s just 10 minutes per day. For lasting consistency, a fitness routine should fit naturally into one’s lifestyle and schedule, Baldwin said. She recommends setting aside kid-free, work-free blocks of time for movement and self-care. Baldwin said she makes time for a daily run as her cardio, which she said helps "work out her lungs." She also incorporates stretching and strength training, which might include physically picking up her kids or toning with weights. She has also started exercising with her children as a way to blend family time with physical activity. DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE The instructor emphasized consistency without overcommitment, noting that doing too much, too soon can lead to burnout. "If something's overwhelming, we're not going to do it," Baldwin said. "Ultimately, we are going to be creatures of habit … we are going do what we feel like needs to get done – but starting to think of a workout more like brushing our teeth is really important." "People are not moving their bodies enough and then we get sick," she went on. "So, the question is, can we do a little bit to prevent that? And obviously not everything can be prevented, but we know that we should move our bodies most days." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Baldwin advised against "biting off more than you can chew." For example, instead of running three miles as a response to being frustrated about your fitness goals, try running for just 10 minutes – or run for just two minutes at a time and take walking breaks. "Doing something is better than thinking about it and doing nothing," she added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The fitness instructor also suggested making exercise a family commitment, helping to reinforce that movement and self-care are priorities. "As moms, we [often] put ourselves last," she said. "Everybody says put your oxygen mask on first, but we don't do that." "I think showing our children that we are human and we are worth taking care of is really important – not just for our relationship with them, but how they will treat themselves when they're older." When life gets busy, she said, it’s easy to make excuses for not working out. Baldwin admitted that on most days, especially in the summer heat, she has "zero interest" in going for a run. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "But I know that I'm not going to regret it," she said. "It’s just about creating the habit and saying, ‘Okay, I'm going to do this, and it's going to be 30 minutes, and I might hate it, but I’m going to be happy to do it.’" Baldwin added, "Showing up is the hardest thing. Once you do it and you create a commitment, it completely changes everything." 'Love yourself' Baldwin encouraged the public, especially women, to tap into how "special and unique each person’s body is." "Start loving yourself and loving your body, no matter what outside opinions you feel like people are directing at you," she said. "Feel capable and feel strong and that you're worth investing in." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Baldwin shared that she herself has struggled "tremendously" with this in her own life. "That is one of the reasons that I show up – to tell my body, ‘I love you, you're worth it.’" She continued, "Nobody has ever existed who is exactly like you, and no one will ever be exactly like you again. So please live every single day cherishing your body, your unique self, and let's have fun and move together."

articles.title: Israel accused of using kites as pretext to justify escalating Gaza attacks
articles.summary: Israel has threatened Palestinian groups against launching ‘kites, drones, and balloons’ from the war-torn enclave.
articles.body:
A four-year-old child was among three Palestinians killed in Israeli air attacks in central Gaza on Sunday, as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatened to escalate attacks over the alleged launching of paper kites from the war-torn enclave.

On Sunday, Israel fired missiles at a warehouse in az-Zawayda, reducing it to rubble, and then carried out strikes near Salah al-Din Street, killing four-year-old Muhammad Abdel Salam Taha.

list 2 of 2 Israel kills 3 in Gaza as Netanyahu threatens attacks over kite launches

Israeli drone attacks also targeted southern Khan Younis and a tent sheltering displaced people at the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah, resulting in more casualties.

Standing amid the destruction in az-Zawayda, witness Abu Ahmed expressed widespread despair over the relentless violence. “There is no ceasefire; there is nothing. We want solutions; we want to live in peace,” he said.

The deadly bombardment comes as Palestinian and Israeli affairs experts warn that the government is fabricating a security crisis around children’s toys to derail ceasefire agreements, enforce demographic changes and ensure Netanyahu’s political survival.

After the attack, Netanyahu and his Defence Minister Israel Katz issued a joint statement on Sunday threatening severe retaliation over the toys. They also threatened the forced displacement of Palestinians from areas “used as launch sites for kites, drones and balloons”.

“There will be no return to the state of affairs prior to October 7 [2023],” the joint statement said, adding that Israel will not allow Hamas or any other group in Gaza “to threaten our communities again and compromise our citizens’ sense of security”.

The attacks came despite the Israeli military acknowledging that the recovered kites contained no explosives and were simply flown by children. While the joint statement cited “kites, drones, and balloons”, military inspections confirmed finding only 10 paper kites – all completely free of explosives and flown by children in displacement camps.

Palestinian political analyst Hussam Shaheen told Al Jazeera that claims regarding drones being launched from Gaza are fabricated. “It is a false and baseless assertion; it is non-existent. It has been denied, and there is no evidence whatsoever to prove any connection to drones,” he said.

Adel Shadid, an expert on Israeli affairs, told Al Jazeera that the threat is entirely manufactured by Hebrew media under the direction of the military establishment.

“It was clear that there was an intention to invest in and use these paper kites as a pretext, and the whole issue might be fabricated,” Shadid said.

Analysts highlighted the absurdity of Israel’s claims regarding the toys.

Palestinian political analyst Hussam Shaheen told Al Jazeera that the kites are merely a flimsy excuse to avoid political commitments.

“It is inconceivable that a state claiming to be a great power possessing a nuclear arsenal considers a paper kite flown by a Palestinian child a security threat,” Shaheen said.

He further noted the logistical impossibility of the Israeli narrative, pointing out that displaced Palestinians are flying these kites in camps surrounded by invading forces.

“Seventy percent of the Strip is still under the control of the Israeli army, so how can one talk about paper kites penetrating all this space and posing a security threat?” Shaheen added.

The sudden escalation coincides with Israel’s rejection of a United States-backed 15-point ceasefire roadmap that Hamas had already accepted, prompting experts to link the violence directly to the upcoming October elections.

Shaheen highlighted how the political establishment relies on violence for votes, noting that Palestinians are historically used as an electoral card.

“Opinion polls indicate that Netanyahu’s chances of forming a government have become non-existent,” Shadid told Al Jazeera.

Experts emphasise that inflating the threat of paper kites serves a darker strategic goal of reshaping demographic realities on the ground.

“Netanyahu does not need to invent a major issue out of the paper kites; rather, the primary goal is pushing the Palestinians towards displacement and dodging any political commitment,” Shaheen told Al Jazeera.

Suleiman Bisharat, a political researcher, explained that the government deliberately uses these weak excuses to instil a psychological state of fear within Israeli society, rallying domestic support for disproportionate force.

“It is true that we might consider these excuses superficial and weak, but ultimately … Israel ties them to the security equation,” Bisharat told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Always tired? Leaving your ‘loops’ open may be the unexpected cause
articles.summary: Procrastinating on some tasks may feel harmless, but the perpetual mental hum of unfinished business may cause more stress than you realize.
articles.body:
The texts you've ignored, the vacation supplies you still need to order, the hard conversation you've been avoiding — repeatedly putting off such tasks because they feel too daunting may seem relatively harmless. But the constant mental hum of unfinished business may be more draining than you realize — like your laptop slowing and glitching because you have 90 browser tabs open.

Some people are waking up to that reality, sharing on social media and in podcasts their epiphanies about the countless open "loops" in their lives in need of closing. The buzzy phrase helps them more easily recognize and combat the habit.

As New Yorker Florence Friebe learned about open loops, she began to see the pattern in her own life — for example, via a hole in her jacket pocket that she kept neglecting to fix and remembered every time she dropped her keys or phone into it.

"I could really start seeing how many repetitive thoughts I was carrying, and how much space it was taking," added Friebe, cohost of the podcast "2 Curly Haired Girls With ADHD" — referring not only to the effects of procrastinating on fixing her jacket pocket but also on cleaning and work tasks.

Psychologists who study procrastination say these people are right to address these issues.

The inertia comes from perceiving "the 'cost' of doing the task in terms of time, energy, and emotional fatigue," said Dr. Vara Saripalli, a clinical psychologist in private practice in Chicago, via email. "They aren't thinking about the other negatives that ensue from waiting; they're focused on the present and avoiding unpleasantness in the here and now."

But as Friebe learned, avoidance also can be highly costly, both practically and by taking up energy that could be used for other things, Saripalli added.

Procrastination and chronic stress can eventually take a toll on both your mental and physical health, said Dr. Fuschia Sirois, professor of social and health psychology at Durham University in England. Sirois, a procrastination expert who has been studying the issue for 25 years, is also the author of "Procrastination: What It Is, Why It's a Problem, and What You Can Do About It."

Those impacts include causing or contributing to a weakened immune system, chronic disease, anxiety and digestive issues, low self-esteem and loneliness, Sirois added.

For Lanna, a content creator and Pilates instructor in Germany, procrastination-related worries even caused stomachaches, she said. Lanna requested that CNN use her nickname for privacy.

But for many people, awareness of these impacts doesn't always make taking action easier.

For generally healthy people, habitual procrastination typically boils down to two causes, even if the details differ per individual, experts said: negative emotions associated with certain tasks or with the prospect of those tasks not going well.

Maybe you're delaying replying to a text because you haven't figured out a perfect response, and you have complicated feelings around imperfection. Or maybe you're avoiding a serious talk with a friend because you're people-pleasing or worried you'll be hurt. (You can read more about procrastination "styles" and related tips here .)

Procrastinating on relatively minor things sometimes may stem from a broader societal shift Saripalli has noticed, in which people are less comfortable with finality and losing options, she said. "The simple task of returning a package becomes an internal monologue of, 'What if I change my mind and I can't get this item again? I'm better off holding on to it till I'm sure.'"

On the other hand, you may just have too many responsibilities and need to consider which ones you can forgo. Maybe you're exhausted by other commitments or spending too much time on your phone, which can be a distraction and energy zapper.

Or maybe the cause of your procrastination is more complicated. If you're struggling to overcome procrastination on your own, consider seeing a doctor or therapist to determine whether there's a more serious underlying issue, Sirois said — such as depression, ADHD or an anxiety disorder.

These disorders can make one's tolerance of negative feelings about a task much lower, Sirois added. That, as well as other symptoms, can contribute to people with these disorders being more prone to procrastinate.

In those cases, some coping strategies can help, but they don't cure disorders or replace professional assistance, Sirois said.

That was true for Lanna, who said she has ADHD and autism, and for Friebe. Friebe said she realized that her struggles with procrastination were significantly tied to her ADHD, depression and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome , or PMOS.

"It was almost like I was lacking ingredients," Friebe said. "Once I got diagnosed, it felt like a giant relief."

Awareness of your urges to procrastinate and of the likely consequences can sometimes be enough to help you regulate your emotions, then choose differently.

But some people such as Friebe and Lanna have also sought professional help for their conditions and improved their lifestyle habits. These changes have given them more energy and the confidence to be more efficient.

Seeing a therapist can really be helpful for anyone regardless of whether you have a condition since they can help you deal with pessimistic ideas causing procrastination. Sirois recently released a free, online evidence-based tool kit for that purpose.

Now Friebe schedules free time to tackle whatever tasks she's got at the moment. Doing a job little by little — or styling to-do list tasks that way — has been more effective than anticipating it with the all-or-nothing thinking that can make responsibilities feel daunting. What also helps Lanna is doing activities that rejuvenate her.

And Friebe really means little , even if that feels stupid, she said. She referred to a story she heard of people who wanted to start exercising at a gym driving to the gym, as they were, on the days they had said they wanted to work out — but not going inside.

The next time, those people also put on workout clothes before driving. Next, they went to the gym in their outfits and exercised for only five minutes. "What they were actually building was trust that they were reliable, that they could do it, so then it could accumulate," Friebe said. "Before you knew it, they were working out."

Studies support the effectiveness of such gradual habit-building.

Guilt and shame are the two most common emotions people feel when they procrastinate, Sirois said, which compound the problem and further paralyze you — even though taking action would alleviate all those negative feelings. "Being self-compassionate is actually a more effective way to get oneself back on track," she added.

Acknowledge that you're struggling and what you're feeling, and ask yourself whether the situation at hand will really be that bad. "Often, we anticipate things are going to be much worse than what they are," Sirois said. Even if your attempts don't go well, trust that you can learn how to navigate the fallout and be OK.

Also try to find the meaning in different responsibilities, those interviewed recommended. If you're delaying cleaning your room and beating yourself up about whether your roommate is judging you for the mess, think about the fact that you deserve a clean, cozy space.

Friebe and Lanna consider how productivity might bring them closer to their life purpose or the person they want to be. And if a heart-to-heart goes poorly, even then, the meaning can be that you grew in your ability to handle conflict, and that you have the truth about the relationship and can act accordingly.

If you're avoiding scheduling a doctor's appointment because you don't want to hear their feedback, your health issue exists regardless. So why not get some answers and prevent your problem from worsening? Regardless of the task, think of how relaxed you'll feel and how much time you'll free up for other fun things if you just get it done.

Since Friebe has improved her health and learned what strategies work for her, "the way I speak to myself is completely different," she said.

"I have a better sense of self and identity and self-trust," Friebe added. "My entire life has changed. I'm a different person."

articles.title: Anti-aging supplements taken by millions may undermine cancer treatment, study warns
articles.summary: Popular NAD+-boosting supplements like NMN and nicotinamide riboside may shield pancreatic cancer cells from chemotherapy, a new study warns.
articles.body: Over-the-counter anti-aging supplements taken by millions of Americans to boost energy and lessen the side effects of chemotherapy may actually impair cancer treatments, a new study suggests. Researchers at the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine found that popular vitamin B3 derivatives – including nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide (NAM) – could help cancer cells survive chemotherapy. Those compounds are used by the body to produce NAD+, a molecule that helps cells generate energy and repair damage. IV THERAPY AND SUPPLEMENTS UNDER SCRUTINY AS EXPERTS WARN OF POTENTIAL SIDE EFFECTS The study, published in the journal Cancer Letters, examined how these supplements interact with treatments for pancreatic cancer, a particularly deadly form of the disease with a 13% five-year survival rate, according to the American Cancer Society. While boosting NAD+ levels through dietary supplements can offer health benefits to non-cancerous cells, pancreatic cancer cells may exploit the extra resources to repair damage caused by chemotherapy and avoid cell death, the researchers found. In both laboratory settings and animal models, the supplements shielded cancer cells against three common chemotherapy drugs: oxaliplatin, 5-fluorouracil and gemcitabine. As a result, tumors survived chemotherapy doses that typically would prove fatal to them. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Our findings highlight a potentially concerning role for NAD+-boosting supplements in the context of active cancer, especially when used in conjunction with chemotherapy," said study lead Jordan Winter, a professor at Case Western Reserve School of Medicine and co-leader of the developmental therapeutics program at the Case Comprehensive Cancer Center, in the press release. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Our discovery is a call to action for the medical community." The study notes that these B3 derivatives are not considered dangerous for healthy individuals using them for general wellness. However, the risk becomes significant for patients currently undergoing active cancer therapy. "This research is a critical reminder that ‘natural’ doesn’t always mean safe, especially in the complex biology of cancer treatment," Winter added. In light of the findings, the research team recommends that oncology teams begin routinely screening patients for supplement use. They also called for more studies into how NAD+ precursors interact with cancer therapies. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Winter urged patients currently in treatment to consult their oncologists before taking any over-the-counter supplements. Because the study relied on laboratory cell cultures and animal models, the findings may not directly translate to how human patients process these supplements during treatment, the team noted. Additionally, the research focused exclusively on pancreatic cancer, meaning the supplements may not have the same effect on chemotherapy for other cancer types or with different drug combinations. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The study also only evaluated short-term cellular responses under controlled laboratory conditions and not human clinical trials, so it remains unclear how these supplements could affect cancer patients over time. Fox News Digital reached out to multiple NAD+ supplement manufacturers for comment.

articles.title: HPV home-testing kits now available for women who have missed cervical screening
articles.summary: Nearly four million women in England can order a self-testing kits to check for high-risk HPV.
articles.body:
Women who have missed a cervical screening appointment in England are to be offered HPV self-testing kits by the NHS.

Over the next year, nearly four million will receive invites on the NHS App or via text message, email or letter to order a free kit to use at home.

Figures show around a third of women who are eligible cervical cancer screening have not taken up the offer recently.

The self-testing kits are designed to get more women checked for high-risk HPV virus, which causes nearly all cases of cervical cancer.

Gem Sofianos-Boorman, 39, said her experience shows how important the screening is.

She was diagnosed with cervical cancer at 28, following screening, and says it was the last thing she expected, given she was young, healthy and had no symptoms.

She had surgery to remove the cancerous cells plus lymph nodes from her abdomen and pelvis to stop it spreading.

"Looking back, I truly believe that going to my screening appointment saved my life. My cancer was found early, which allowed me to have treatment before it spread.

"That's why it's great news that the NHS is making it more accessible for some people to take part in screening."

Cervical cancer often doesn't cause any symptoms until the disease is more advanced and harder to treat.

"If you receive an invite to cervical screening, or an offer of a self-testing kit, please don't ignore it - it could save your life."

Dr Sue Mann, national clinical director for women's health, said: "Offering millions of women an alternative test they can do from the comfort of their own homes will be a game-changer â making it easier than ever for them to get tested.

"There are lots of reasons that may stop women from getting their cervical screening â embarrassment, lack of time or worries about discomfort â and these kits provide a discreet and convenient option we hope will encourage more women to take up the life-saving test."

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper added: "Cervical cancer is preventable - but that's why we want to make it as easy and convenient as possible for women to keep up with their screening."

The kits contain a swab, similar to a long cotton, bud which is used to collect a sample from the vagina.

It is then sent back to the NHS and if high-risk HPV is found, individuals will be invited to book a follow-up cervical screening appointment.

High-risk HPV increases the risk of cervical cancer, but it does not mean a woman will automatically develop it.

Trials of the self-testing in London suggest it could lead to one in 10 women to come forward for screening â boosting uptake by around 400,000 a year.

Other parts of the UK are also looking at introducing self-testing.

Women aged 24 to 64 are invited for cervical screening every five years â or more frequently if HPV is detected.

Through a combination of HPV vaccination, which is offered to teenagers, and improved screening, the NHS is hoping to eliminate cervical cancer by 2040.

The NHS says cervical screening appointments with a clinician is still the best way to prevent cancer â and even if you have missed an appointment you can still come forward for one.

articles.title: Morre uma vítimas de explosão que atingiu três casas na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Falecimento de Diana Guimarães dos Santos da Silva, de 42 anos, foi confirmado pela família nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.summary: Falecimento de Diana Guimarães dos Santos da Silva, de 42 anos, foi confirmado pela família nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.body:
Uma das vítimas da explosão que atingiu três casas na cidade de Santo Antônio de Jesus , no Recôncavo da Bahia, faleceu nesta terça-feira (25), em Salvador . Diana Guimarães dos Santos da Silva , de 42 anos, estava internada Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE) desde a última quarta-feira (19), quando o acidente aconteceu. A informação foi confirmado por familiares.

Segundo informações apuradas pela TV Bahia, ela morreu após complicações durante uma cirurgia. Diana da Silva teve queimaduras de terceiro grau em várias partes do corpo. Ainda não há detalhes sobre o sepultamento dela.

📲 Clique aqui e entre no grupo do WhatsApp do g1 Feira de Santana e região

A filha dela, Thalita Santos de Andrade, de 13 anos, também está internada no HGE. Ela ainda não sabe do falecimento da mãe. Segundo informações apuradas pela TV Bahia, o quadro de saúde da adolescente é considerado estável.

Morre uma das três vítimas de explosão que atingiu três casas no interior da Bahia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Bahia

Uma terceira vítima da explosão, identificada como Elóisa Silva, de 9 anos, está internada em hospital de Santo Antônio de Jesus. Não há detalhes sobre o estado de saúde dela.

A explosão aconteceu em uma região de Santo Antônio de Jesus conhecida como Casco. A suspeita inicial é de que ela tenha sido provocada pelo vazamento de um botijão de gás. Segundo a Defesa Civil, um laudo de perícia será realizado para determinar as causas do acidente. Informações iniciais indicam que a mangueira do botijão estava vencida desde 2019.

Botijão de gás causou explosão e três casas foram atingidas em Santo Antônio de Jesus — Foto: Tino Alves

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado por volta das 5h e encaminhou uma das vítimas para o Hospital Regional de Santo Antônio de Jesus (HRSAJ). As outras duas foram socorridas anteriormente por equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros, com apoio de moradores, e também levadas para a unidade de saúde.

Elóisa Silva, de 9 anos, teve queimaduras nas pernas e no rosto, além de uma fratura no fêmur. De acordo com familiares, ela estava passando a noite na casa da amiga, Thalita Santos de Andrade, de 13 anos, quando a explosão aconteceu.

A adolescente de 13 anos também sofreu queimaduras e passou por cirurgia. Familiares informaram que ela está estável e também não corre risco de morte. Já Diana da Silva, mãe da jovem, teve queimaduras de terceiro grau pelo corpo, passou por um procedimento cirúrgico e foi transferida para o HGE.

Segundo familiares, a mulher morava sozinha com a filha e havia se mudado para o imóvel, que era alugado, há cerca de oito dias.Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros estiveram no local para atender à ocorrência. A situação das casas vizinhas também deverá ser avaliada.

articles.title: Influenciadora esfaqueia suspeito de abusar da filha em Franca, SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ninguém foi preso. O boletim de ocorrência registra a apreensão de um canivete e aponta que a mulher também ficou ferida. A Polícia Civil apura a lesão e a denúncia de estupro de vulnerável.
articles.summary: A Polícia Civil de Franca investiga a lesão corporal e a denúncia de estupro de vulnerável após a apreensão de um canivete usado pela mulher contra o suspeito de 41 anos.
articles.body:
Uma influenciadora de 25 anos feriu com um canivete um homem de 41 anos que ela acusa de ter abusado sexualmente da filha dela, de 5 anos, na manhã de segunda-feira (24), em Franca (SP). O caso foi registrado como lesão corporal.

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a ocorrência foi às 9h55 na Avenida Major Nicácio, no bairro Cidade Nova, em frente à loja onde uma tia de Laryssa Campanati Pereira trabalha. Maikel Wilker Martins, suspeito de ter cometido o abuso, foi socorrido e levado à Santa Casa.

Ninguém foi preso. O documento registra que não houve prisão em flagrante. A mulher também sofreu lesões nas costas, nos braços, nas mãos e nas pernas e foi encaminhada ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML) para exame.

A acusação de abuso sexual contra a criança foi registrada na Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Franca e é apurada em investigação separada. Ele não foi preso, indiciado nem denunciado.

O g1 tentou localizar a defesa de Maikel Wilker Martins, mas não tinha conseguido até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Influenciadora golpeou com um canivete o marido da tia que é suspeito de abusar a filha de 5 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Faça parte do canal do g1 Ribeirão e Franca no WhatsApp

Segundo o documento, a mulher relatou à polícia que a filha lhe contou no dia 21 de agosto ter sido abusada sexualmente pelo homem. Ela afirmou que tentou contato com os dois conselhos tutelares da cidade e que não recebeu respaldo. Ao g1 , o conselho disse não ter recebido contato.

Ainda de acordo com o relato registrado, ela foi até a loja para contar à tia o que havia acontecido. No local, o homem teria se aproximado perguntando se ela "já sabia o que ocorrera", ido até o próprio veículo e voltado em direção a ela.

A mulher disse à polícia que, ao perceber que ele iria pegá-la à força, tirou um canivete da bolsa e desferiu um golpe. Em seguida, segundo o boletim, ele a pressionou com o próprio corpo contra o braço de um banco, e ela relatou ter desferido outros golpes em legítima defesa, enquanto pedia socorro.

O canivete foi apreendido e lacrado. A mulher informou à polícia que acredita haver câmeras de monitoramento no local. A tese de legítima defesa é a versão dela e ainda será apurada.

O homem não compareceu à delegacia porque estava em atendimento na Santa Casa. O boletim foi registrado, segundo a autoridade policial, para melhor apuração dos fatos.

Três dias entre a denúncia e o registro policial

Segundo a defesa, a criança relatou o abuso na sexta-feira (21), e o caso teria ocorrido no domingo anterior (16). A mulher levou a filha para atendimento médico no mesmo dia, e o laudo do exame foi entregue à delegacia, segundo a advogada.

A advogada afirma que a família foi informada de que a Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher de Franca funciona apenas de segunda a sexta-feira, até as 17h, e que deveria procurar o Conselho Tutelar na segunda-feira.

O registro do abuso na DDM só foi feito na segunda-feira (24), mesmo dia da agressão, de acordo com os documentos.

Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Franca (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

Conselho Tutelar diz que atende 24 horas

Procurado pelo g1, o Conselho Tutelar de Franca afirmou que funciona em regime ininterrupto. "Nós atendemos 24 horas", disse uma conselheira.

Segundo o órgão, o caso só chegou ao seu conhecimento por volta das 12h de segunda-feira, pelas redes sociais, e o boletim registrado na DDM foi encaminhado ao Conselho às 14h24 do mesmo dia. Até então, não havia registro próprio sobre o caso.

O Conselho afirma que tentou contato com a mãe, sem sucesso até a entrevista, e que vai avaliar a aplicação de medidas de proteção à criança.

A lesão corporal é apurada pela Polícia Civil, e o boletim registra orientação sobre o prazo de seis meses para o oferecimento de representação criminal. A denúncia de estupro de vulnerável corre em separado, na Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher.

Denúncias de violência contra crianças e adolescentes podem ser feitas pelo Disque 100, gratuito e anônimo. Casos de violência contra a mulher podem ser denunciados pelo 180.

Nesta terça-feira (25), sete dos oito candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco nas eleições de 2026 participaram de atos de campanha. Entre as atividades, estão caminhadas, campanha "porta a porta", gravação de propaganda eleitoral e participação em sabatinas e entrevistas.

O candidato do PSOL concedeu entrevista para a emissora de rádio Nossa Voz FM durante a manhã. Na sequência, ele gravou material para TV e redes sociais.

À noite, o candidato participou de um ato com artistas na Casa Mariele Franco, no bairro do Derby, área central do Recife.

O ex-prefeito do Recife participou de um encontro com mães de crianças com autismo na UPAE do bairro da Cohab, na Zona Sul da capital. Durante a atividade, ele prometeu atenção criar uma rede de centros TEA em todas as regiões do estado .

Durante a tarde, o candidato do PSB participou de sabatina promovida pelo jornal Diario de Pernambuco, no bairro de Santo Amaro, área central do Recife.

À noite, por volta das 19h, João Campos realizou uma caminhada pelas ruas do bairro de Santo Aleixo, em Jaboatão dos Guararapes, no Grande Recife. Por fim, o candidato do PSB compareceu à inauguração do comitê de um candidato a deputado estadual do Podemos , partido que não faz parte da coligação dele.

O candidato do Democrata teve três atos públicos de campanha nesta terça. Pela manhã, participou de reunião de lideranças na cidade de Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, no Agreste do estado.

À tarde, Professor Jeremias se encontrou com aliados no município de Toritama, no Agreste. À noite, o candidato finalizou a agenda com uma nova reunião com lideranças de Limoeiro, na mesma região.

A candidata da Unidade Popular conversou com trabalhadores de uma fábrica de pipoca e, na sequência, participou de sabatina dos candidatos ao governo na TV Universitária, no bairro de Santo Amaro, no centro da capital.

À noite, Professora Camila fez um ato de "porta-porta" no bairro do Totó, na Zona Oeste do Recife, onde conversou com moradores.

A governadora e candidata à reeleição participou de uma panfletagem em frente ao Hospital da Restauração, no bairro do Derby, área central do Recife. Raquel Lyra prometeu reestruturar grandes hospitais e regionalizar atendimento de saúde .

No fim da tarde, Raquel Lyra gravou material para o guia eleitoral do rádio.

O candidato do Missão realizou nesta terça os atos que foram cancelados pela sua campanha na segunda-feira (24). À tarde, ele visitou o centro de Paulista , no Grande Recife, onde se encontrou com a militância do partido e gravou material para as redes sociais.

Na sequência, Renan Hallais teve encontro com a militância na cidade de Abreu e Lima , também no Grande Recife, e depois partiu para a cidade de Goiana , na Zona da Mata Norte, onde apresentou propostas e gravou mais material para as redes sociais.

No início da tarde, o candidato do PCO participou de um programa ao vivo online promovido pelo canal da Rádio Causa Operária no YouTube, com o candidato a presidente pelo partido, Rui Costa Pimenta .

À tarde, Victor Assis participou de reunião com integrantes de sua campanha. Durante a noite, o candidato participou ao vivo de um plenária nacional, online, com militantes e candidatos do PCO de todo o Brasil, de acordo com sua assessoria.

articles.title: Mulher é baleada por ex-marido após ele desrespeitar medida protetiva | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima estava trabalhando quando foi atingida por dois disparos. Ela está internada. Após o crime, homem tentou se suicidar. Ele também foi levado ao hospital.
articles.summary: Vítima estava trabalhando quando foi atingida por dois disparos. Ela está internada. Após o crime, homem tentou se suicidar. Ele também foi levado ao hospital.
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 20 anos foi baleada pelo ex-marido na tarde desta segunda-feira (25), depois que ele descumpriu a medida protetiva que ela tinha contra ele e foi até o salão de beleza dela, em Curitiba .

A mulher estava trabalhando quando foi baleada pelo homem. Segundo a Guarda Municipal, ele disparou duas vezes contra a mulher e, em seguida, tentou se suicidar.

"Eu escutei um grito, três tiros, saí na porta e vi a dona do salão cambaleando e caindo no chão", relata a pedagoga Ana Cristina de Araújo.

Uma equipe da Guarda Municipal que estava perto foi abordada por populares, foi até o local e constatou que ambos estavam vivos e acionou o Siate (Serviço Integrado de Atendimento ao Trauma em Emergência).

A mulher foi levada ao Hospital Evangélico Mackenzie e o homem ao Hospital do Trabalhador. As instituições não informaram o estado de saúde deles.

O g1 optou por não dar o nome dos envolvidos para proteger a identidade da mulher.

Um dos tiros disparados pelo homem chegou a atingir um apartamento vizinho ao prédio. O projétil atingiu uma televisão que fica dentro do quarto de uma criança, mas que estava vazio no momento do crime.

Crime: Moradores estranham sumiço de vizinhos e latidos de cachorro, entram em apartamento e encontram pai, mãe e filho mortos

Bebê encontrada em sacola de lixo: Criança chegou ao hospital com hipotermia e duas fraturas, mas estado de saúde é estável

articles.title: Raquel Lyra propõe reestruturar grandes hospitais e regionalizar saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidata do PSD à reeleição cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Derby, na área central do Recife, nesta terça (25).
articles.summary: Candidata do PSD à reeleição cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Derby, na área central do Recife, nesta terça (25).
articles.body:
A governadora Raquel Lyra , candidata à reeleição pelo PSD , cumpriu agenda de campanha no bairro do Derby, na área central do Recife , na tarde desta terça-feira (25). Ela realizou um ato de panfletagem e prometeu, caso seja reeleita, reestruturar e ampliar grandes hospitais, além de aproximar o atendimento de saúde da população (veja vídeo acima) .

A candidata escolheu a Avenida Agamenon Magalhães, próximo ao Hospital da Restauração, que está em reforma desde 2024. Na chegada ao local, ela cumprimentou eleitores, tirou fotos, gravou vídeos e distribuiu adesivos e panfletos para motoristas e motociclistas.

✅ Receba no WhatsApp as notícias do g1 PE

A candidata do PSD esteve acompanhada de Priscila Krause (PSD), candidata a vice, e de Eduardo da Fonte (PP), candidato ao Senado. Durante a agenda, ela conversou com jornalistas e detalhou seus planos para expandir serviços de saúde com foco em regionalização.

"Além de reestruturação dos todos os nossos grandes hospitais, que já estão em reforma e ampliação, [faremos] a entrega dos nossos quatro hospitais da mulher, do Hospital Mestre Dominguinhos, as ampliações que são novos hospitais no Procape, no Otávio de Freitas, no Hospital Regional do Agreste, e mais do que tudo a saúde mais perto de casa, com regionalização e resolutividade onde as pessoas vivem", afirmou.

articles.title: Arizona grandpa to undergo amputation after collapsing on scorching sidewalk
articles.summary: A 72-year-old man collapsed on a 120-degree sidewalk in Arizona and suffered severe burns that will require above-knee amputation of his leg.
articles.body: An Arizona grandfather is preparing to undergo an above-knee amputation of his right leg after he tripped and fell while walking outside in Bullhead City during 120-degree heat earlier this month, according to his family. Grant Siler, 72, fell during a walk on Aug. 3 in Bullhead City, causing his body temperature to rise to more than 105 degrees. The family’s GoFundMe said Siler was on the ground for an estimated at least an hour before a passerby found him. The fundraiser said he suffered second and third-degree burns in multiple areas of his body, heat stroke and multiple organ shock. HIKERS FACE URGENT GRAND CANYON HEAT WARNING AFTER TEEN’S DEATH ON POPULAR TRAIL He was then taken to a burn ICU in Las Vegas, where he has been cared for since the incident. When he arrived at the facility, doctors discovered he was suffering from heat stroke and organ shock. "He is in constant pain, can barely move, and has undergone two debridements. Also, he will soon need to undergo surgery for amputation, the extent is not yet known," the GoFundMe reads. During surgery, a surgeon found that tissue in Siler’s right leg was so severely damaged it was unlikely to fully heal, according to an update posted to the fundraiser. Siler is scheduled to have his right leg amputated above the knee on Aug. 31, according to FOX 10 Phoenix. ESPN ANALYST MATT MILLER SAYS HE UNDERWENT LIFE-SAVING AMPUTATION OF LEFT ARM AFTER CAR ACCIDENT "The plan now is to have an above-knee amputation. The Dr's feel he will overall heal faster and have better pain control this way," the fundraiser reads. "We can all imagine that after any amputation, the road to recovery is long and hard...physically, mentally and emotionally," it continued. His wife, Vicki, has been traveling one-and-a-half-hours each way to be with her husband as she continuing to work to support the family’s financial obligations. The family said the couple will also soon have to face medical bills to help with Siler’s recovery. The family is accepting donations to help with home renovations, home medical supplies, prosthetics and other added costs. "He's hurting really bad," Crook told FOX 10. "He's the 'get up and walk it off' type." "So for him to holler out in pain … it’s really hard to hear. That’s not the kind of person that he is," she added.
